messages:
sam: FYI, getting an unusual surge of GPU errors in eu-central-1 over the last 10m, causing a bunch of nodes to auto-drain. Capacity down ~28%.
irene: seeing the same. error stream looks like a mix of parity/ECC traces and driver timeouts.
jay: @oncall can you confirm if this is hardware-level or driver side? any recent driver rollouts to the region?
oncall: no driver rollouts in eu-central-1 in the last 24h. infra-bot: alert: 18 nodes marked UNHEALTHY in eu-central-1/gpu-pool-3 (last 8m).
mike: grabbing logs from one of the drained hosts now. attaching snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T12:01:02Z] gpu0: cecc_parity_error count=5
[2026-03-17T12:01:03Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, reason: TLB or page fault?
nvml: failed to query processes: Unknown error
```
dana: perf counters show elevated correctable ECC and frequent slot resets. not all cards are affected, looks clustered by rack.
irene: rack-level issue could point to power/PSU or PCIe switch flakiness. any recent maintenance in that AZ?
oncall: ops says no scheduled maintenance. power alarms started around 11:50 UTC in a subset of hosts.
sam: that's interesting — power blips -> transient parity errors -> driver trips -> autoscale drains. we should isolate the rack and force-skip for scheduling.
jay: agreed. i'll push a quick routing rule to avoid scheduling to gpu-pool-3 racks in eu-central-1: ```
PATCH /routing/policies/avoid
{ "region": "eu-central-1", "pool": "gpu-pool-3", "rack_tags": ["rck-11","rck-12","rck-13"], "duration": "2h" }
```
irene: also enabling more permissive fallback to lower-capacity model variants in eu region so latencies don't spike.
mike: i'm provisioning 6 extra nodes in eu-west-1 and kicking a cross-region placement so running jobs can migrate. ETA ~9m for warm nodes.
oncall: temporary scaling and routing applied. infra-bot: action_taken: routing rule deployed by jay, 6 warm nodes requested by mike.
sam: for triage — collect dmesg + smi logs and the PCIe topology from affected hosts. priority: determine if firmware/PSU change needed.
dana: grabbing dmesg, but initial look shows repeated `pcieport 0000:65:00: AER: Corrected error` and `EDAC MC0: CE` entries.
jay: can we confirm if the vendor rolled any firmware? reaching out to colo with vendor ticket.
oncall: opened ticket #CO-2026-1745 with vendor, they acknowledged and asked for SM logs.
irene: low-risk mitigation: increase driver retry thresholds and lengthen node health check grace window from 30s->90s to avoid noisy auto-drains while we investigate. any objections?
mike: fine with temporary health window increase, but we must track cost impact of longer retry loops.
sam: do it. also add a metric alert if corrective ECC per-card > 3 in 5m so we can trigger immediate isolation before widespread drains.
infra-bot: metric_alert_rule created by irene: gpu.correctable_ecc > 3 for 5m -> notify #eng-runtime and auto-isolate.
dana: putting together a short runbook for the on-call with checklist: collect logs, soft-reset GPU, power-cycle host if persists, replace card if persistent after reboot.
jay: vendor confirmed they've seen PSU flakiness on ~10 racks in the colo region and are dispatching techs to inspect. ETA on physical inspection 4-6 hours.
sam: long term we may need to avoid that colo until firmware/PSU fix. start cost calc for cross-region warm pools to maintain headroom.
mike: running a rough cost estimate: +18% infra cost if we keep extra warm nodes for 24h across us/eu. will post numbers in a follow-up.
oncall: current user impact: 12% request retries and a small spike in 5xxs for some latency-sensitive routes. fallbacks active.
irene: ok. next steps: 1) avoid scheduling to affected racks (done), 2) extend health check grace (sam), 3) provision cross-region warm nodes (mike), 4) vendor inspection (jay), 5) add metric alert and runbook (irene/dana).
sam: thanks — keep updates here. if anything changes faster than every 10m ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
